newsitem.title: USA: East Coast refiners still unaffected by hurricane.
newsitem.headline: East Coast refiners still unaffected by hurricane.

text.p: U.S. East Coast refiners continued to monitor the situation but had not cut runs or shipments ahead of the approaching hurricane, expected to make landfall along the South Carolina Coast this evening, according to oil company spokesmen.

Amoco Corp's Yorktown refinery, the closest significant-sized plant in the path of Hurricane Fran's eye, is operating normally and had not suspended oil product shipments, a company spokesman said Thursday.
"At this point there has been no impact on operations, and to our knowledge, no impact on shipping," said Mike Brien for Amoco.
Amoco halted products shipments from the 50,000 barrel per day (bpd) Yorktown refinery during Hurricane Bertha in July.
Ahead of Hurricane Fran, with sustained winds of up to 115 miles per hour (185 kmh), ports from Savannah, Georgia, to Charleston, South Carolina were shut to vessel traffic.
In Virginia, a Marine Safety Office official said ports in the Norfolk area and Delaware River Bay remained open.
Ships were being advised, however, to take precautionary measures against rough seas in the next 24 to 36 hours.

Other major refineries in the area such as Star Enterprise's Delaware City refinery (140,000 bpd), Sun Co's refineries in Philadelphia, Pa. (307,000 bpd) and Marcus Hook, N.J. (175,000 bpd), are only closely tracking the storm.
"It has not affected our operations, and it's not expected to," Bud Davis, spokesman for Sun Co said, adding that ships were presently out at sea manoeuvring away from the storm.
Officials at Tosco Corp's 230,000 bpd Linden refinery, and Coastal Corp's 130,000 bpd Eagle Point refineries in N.J., also reported no disruptions.
Oil markets, meanwhile, were unimpressed by the potential threat of Hurricane Fran noting there were not many refineries located in the southern portion of the U.S. East Coast.
"Fran is a nasty storm, but not an oil event," one Texas trader said.
